svg.title: Compare Rebate Yields on Eligible Settled Purchase Dollars
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-eligible-card-rebate-yields; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Rebate Yields on Eligible Settled Purchase Dollars; subtitle: Five illustrative payment-rail cases use one denominator.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Bars are hypothetical contractual rebate rates inside the supplied 2%–4% range, not named issuer offers or observed market averages. Each rate uses eligible settled purchase spend before interest, fees and clawbacks. Uncapped treatment requires express issuer terms; these rates do not derive the 35% portfolio retained share.; caption: At $10,000 eligible spend, these cases produce $200–$400 of rebates before costs. Float is payment timing, not another yield.; stages: label: Buying-group general merchandise; value: 2.0% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 2.0; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $200 of rebates only when resale activity and merchant classification qualify under the actual commercial card agreement.; label: Buying-group electronics orders; value: 2.5% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 2.5; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $250 before card costs. Check electronics exclusions, rebate caps and returns; shipment value does not change the contracted rate.; label: Authorized event ticket inventory; value: 3.0% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 3.0; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $300 only if ticket transactions qualify. Exchange sale proceeds and inventory appreciation are separate from this rebate calculation.; label: Transferable corporate-suite allocations; value: 3.5% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 3.5; detail: A modeled $10,000 card purchase produces $350 before surcharges. Reject the card rail when its incremental cost exceeds the collectible contractual rebate.; label: Issuer-qualified promotional purchases; value: 4.0% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 4.0; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $400 within verified offer terms. Replace the rate when promotional periods expire; never extend temporary pricing across the annual model.

text.title: Compare Rebate Yields on Eligible Settled Purchase Dollars
text.tspan: Compare Rebate Yields on Eligible Settled Purchase

rect.title: label: Buying-group general merchandise; value: 2.0% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 2.0; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $200 of rebates only when resale activity and merchant classification qualify under the actual commercial card agreement.

label: Buying-group electronics orders; value: 2.5% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 2.5; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $250 before card costs. Check electronics exclusions, rebate caps and returns; shipment value does not change the contracted rate.

label: Authorized event ticket inventory; value: 3.0% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 3.0; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $300 only if ticket transactions qualify. Exchange sale proceeds and inventory appreciation are separate from this rebate calculation.

label: Transferable corporate-suite allocations; value: 3.5% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 3.5; detail: A modeled $10,000 card purchase produces $350 before surcharges. Reject the card rail when its incremental cost exceeds the collectible contractual rebate.

label: Issuer-qualified promotional purchases; value: 4.0% rebate on eligible settled purchases; numeric value: 4.0; detail: A modeled $10,000 purchase produces $400 within verified offer terms. Replace the rate when promotional periods expire; never extend temporary pricing across the annual model.

text.title: Assumptions: Bars are hypothetical contractual rebate rates inside the supplied 2%–4% range, not named issuer offers or observed market averages. Each rate uses eligible settled purchase spend before interest, fees and clawbacks. Uncapped treatment requires express issuer terms; these rates do not derive the 35% portfolio retained share.
